how_it_wins:
Sai, Master Thopterist stays in the command zone and the 99 holds 43 artifact spells. Every one you cast is two artifacts: the spell and a 1/1 flying Thopter. Stack 001 proves the order. Sai's trigger goes on the stack above the spell and resolves first, so the Thopter is on the battlefield before the artifact is, and one Chief of the Foundry cast takes Master of Etherium from 1/1 to 4/4. That is the deck: the count climbs by two per cast, and the count is what Master, Darksteel Juggernaut, Broodstar, Nettlecyst and Adaptive Omnitool read.

Three things have to be true. Sai on the battlefield: the goldfish casts him on turn 3 in 8,968 of 10,000 games and by turn 6 in 99.7%. Cheap artifacts in hand: a rock, a Myr or a cost reducer is drawn by turn 6 in 82.5% of games, the draw suite in 95.1%. A scaler or a connector: a count payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 77.0%, but THE KILL pair, a big body AND an anthem, Steel Overseer or Whirler Rogue, is 43.4% by turn 6 and 67.4% ever, and the diagnostic reads the engine online 36.7% by turn 5 and 66.7% by turn 10. The connector is the thin leg. Stack 002 shows why it matters: two Thopters made this turn pay Whirler Rogue's cost and Myr Battlesphere cannot be blocked.

The clock, with no Thopters counted: median kill turn 10, 4.0% by turn 8, 48.9% of games with no kill by turn 10, mean bodies 2.567 by turn 6. Sai's trigger and his {1}{U} sacrifice-two draw are not modelled, so every board and damage figure is a floor. The deck is still the slow seat, and it is meant to be: floor Bracket 1, target 2, DeckCheck 30/96.

What the table misreads is the count, not the Thopters. A 1/1 flier is nothing; each one after it is +1/+1 on whatever Nettlecyst holds, +1 on Juggernaut and +1 on Master, all at once. The turn a lord lands on six artifacts the board moves by more than the lord's own power, and that is the turn to attack, not the turn after. Until then make bodies, hold {U}{U}, and let the seat with the bigger creature take the table's removal.
mulligan:
The goldfish keeps a seven with two to five lands and ships the rest: 84.1% of sevens kept, a mean of 0.185 mulligans, and 88.7% of its keeps can act by turn 3. The land rule is yours too. In 10,000 sevens, 231 had no land and 1,186 had one; 175 had six or seven. Ship all of those.

Sai is free, so every hand has the engine and no hand has the payoff until a count payoff lands. Judge a keep on what you cast on turns 2, 4 and 5 around a turn-3 Sai. Count the artifact spells at mana value three or less (25 of the 43) and the accelerants: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Mind Stone, Thought Vessel, Silver Myr, Ornithopter of Paradise, Palladium Myr, Hedron Archive, Cultivator's Caravan, Etherium Sculptor, Foundry Inspector. One of those eleven is in 57.4% of sevens and drawn by turn 6 in 82.5% of games.

Keep three lands, one accelerant and two cheap artifacts. Keep two lands with a two-mana rock, because the rock is a land that also makes a Thopter. The model keeps any two-lander (3,158 of its 10,000 keeps) and hits its turn-3 drop 93.7% of the time, but by turn 5 the hit rate is 76.5%, so a two-lander with no rock is a ship. That rule is mine, not the model's. Keep Vedalken Archmage or Master of Etherium with a rock: that is the engine stage in one hand.

Ship lands plus Myr Battlesphere, Graaz, Steel Hellkite and Kappa Cannoneer with nothing under four. That is the payoff with no enabler, and a payoff without the engine is a blank until the count exists. Ship a hand whose only spells are Counterspell, Negate and Aetherize. The deck's answers are drawn by turn 6 in 85.4% of games anyway, and a hand that holds mana up on turns 2 to 4 never starts the count. Commander's free first mulligan costs nothing; spend it on a hand that has lands and nothing to cast with them.

combo_lines.001: The line turns on one ordering rule: a cast trigger goes on the stack above the spell that caused it and resolves first (CR 603.3, 405.5). So the Thopter is a permanent before Chief of the Foundry is, and nothing about Chief's resolution changes that. What it proves: one artifact cast adds two artifacts to your count. Master of Etherium reads the board, not the stack. It is 1/1 while Chief is a spell, 2/2 with the Thopter in, 3/3 once Chief lands, 4/4 under Chief's anthem, so Master grows by three off a three-mana cast. The Thopter ends 3/3 and Chief 3/4. Sai stays 1/4; he is a Human, not an artifact, and no anthem here reaches him. What it does not prove: what happens if Chief is countered with the trigger above it (needs a stack scenario), whether Kappa Cannoneer takes one counter from the Thopter and another from the spell (an open question in the engine), and what Vedalken Archmage draws on the same cast (needs a stack scenario). Use it as the deck's basic arithmetic: before you cast, count your artifacts, add two, and that is Master's and Darksteel Juggernaut's size when the stack is empty.
combo_lines.002: The line turns on what CR 302.6 restricts and what it leaves alone. Summoning sickness stops a creature's own {T} or {Q} ability and stops it attacking; it says nothing about a cost worded 'Tap two untapped artifacts you control'. Whirler Rogue's cost has no tap symbol, so two Thopters Sai made this turn pay it, and by the same reading Rogue's own age is irrelevant: it can make something unblockable the turn it lands off its own two Thopters. What it proves: Myr Battlesphere, under your control since last turn, cannot be blocked this combat; Rogue stays untapped and may attack; the two tapped Thopters cannot pay a second activation (118.3), so a second target needs two more untapped artifacts. What it does not prove: combat damage, Battlesphere's attack trigger and how many Myr to tap (an open question in the engine), and the same play aimed at Darksteel Juggernaut. The engine keeps that line dashed because 002 never names the Juggernaut (needs a stack scenario). Use it as THE KILL's connector: cast two artifact spells precombat, tap the two fresh Thopters, and send the count-sized body at the seat that could otherwise block it.
combo_lines.003: The line turns on two words on the Disk, 'Destroy all', and on who it reaches. Indestructible stops destroy (CR 702.12b), so Darksteel Juggernaut and Darksteel Citadel stay; nothing else of yours does. Hexproof stops targeting (702.11b), and 'Destroy all artifacts, creatures, and enchantments' targets nothing, so Padeem protects nothing here and dies with the board. What it proves: the Disk destroys itself, Sai, Padeem and every Thopter; Sai may go to the command zone as a state-based action (704.6d) and costs {2} more for each previous command-zone cast (903.8); the Thopters cease to exist in the graveyard; and Juggernaut's size is read after the event, not before. It is 2/2, counting itself and the Citadel. What it does not prove: All Is Dust's board. The engine enumerates 19 coloured permanents that would go and every Thopter that would stay, but that is argued, not proved (needs a stack scenario). Nor whether you can sacrifice two artifacts to Sai with the Disk's ability on the stack (needs a stack scenario). Use it as the price list for the symmetric button: press it when a 2/2 and your lands beat what the table keeps.

threat_assessment:
Nothing here is played; there is no captain's log for this deck. It is argued from the engine, the goldfish and the oracle text.

The table ignores you while the board is Sai, rocks and 1/1 fliers. That ends on a countable event: a count payoff lands on six or more artifacts. Master of Etherium, Chief of the Foundry or Steel Overseer turns every Thopter into a 2/2 or 3/3 at once; Darksteel Juggernaut or Broodstar at eight artifacts is an 8/8; Whirler Rogue with two untapped artifacts makes one of them unblockable (stack 002). The goldfish puts THE KILL pair on the board by turn 6 in 43.4% of games and the diagnostic reads the engine online 36.7% by turn 5, 66.7% by turn 10. When it comes, attack that turn. A board that stabilises and passes gives three opponents a free draw step each.

Your tells, and the order to show them. Scariest last. Cast the rocks, Ichor Wellspring, Mazemind Tome and the Myr first; Thopter Spy Network and Vedalken Archmage read as value; the lords and Rogue are the cards the table removes, so they come down the turn they attack. Hold Master Transmuter with a seven-drop in hand rather than showing both. Fall from Favor makes you the monarch, and the monarch is who gets attacked; cast it behind Propaganda or a Thopter wall, not ahead of them.

Their tells. A sorcery-speed sweeper is near-certain across a four-player game, so deploy in waves: commit what wins before the wrath, keep Myr Retriever, Ichor Wellspring and Buried Ruin as the rebuild, and keep two artifacts plus {1}{U} up. Sai's draw has no timing line on the card, so two Thopters become a card with the sweeper on the stack (the Disk-plus-Sai version needs a stack scenario). Nettlecyst, Adaptive Omnitool and Forsaken Monument survive a creature wipe; the three creature lords do not. A wipe that names artifacts is the one that ends the board outright, and the only answer is Counterspell or Negate on the way in. The goldfish has interaction in hand on turn 5 in 80.3% of games and castable in 13.6%, because the model spends the mana. You hold it on purpose. Hold it for the wrath, not for the first big creature.

Open mana. {U}{U} is Counterspell; {1}{U} is Negate or Sai's draw; {3}{U} is Aetherize, which answers an alpha strike from any seat. Shimmer Myr lets you cast the artifacts on the end step with that mana still up. Padeem blanks targeted removal on artifacts but not on Sai, who has no hexproof and no recursion to the command zone; each return costs {2} more.

The reset buttons. Nevinyrral's Disk leaves you Darksteel Juggernaut at 2/2 and the Citadel, nothing else (stack 003). All Is Dust, on oracle text, takes the 19 coloured permanents in the 99 plus Sai and leaves every Thopter, Myr, rock and colourless body: argued, not proved. Press the Disk when the table's board beats yours by more than a 2/2; press All Is Dust when the Thopters are the board.
matchups:
Argued, not played: no game is logged. Each rule below is tied to a card or a figure.

Against a sweeper deck. Assume the wrath. Commit what wins before it and no more. The lords are bodies and die with the board, so lead with Nettlecyst, Adaptive Omnitool or Forsaken Monument when you have the choice and keep one creature lord in hand. The rebuild is cheap because the engine is Sai: every artifact cast after the wipe is a body again, and one recast at {2}{U} plus {2} is a fair rate. Counterspell and Negate are for the wrath. Against a deck whose plan is to buy time, holding back is the loss; attack with the fliers you have.

Against a tax or stax seat. The deck wants two or three artifact spells a turn, and a tax halves that. Etherium Sculptor and Foundry Inspector restore the spell count under a tax; cast them before the tax lands if you see it coming, and protect them after. You do not own the long game under a lock, so you are the beatdown: name the out early. Counterspell and Negate stop a lock piece only on the stack; Meteor Golem and Duplicant answer a resolved creature; All Is Dust takes every coloured piece while your colourless board stays; Steel Hellkite clears one mana value after it connects. Breadth is thin, 3 counters, 2 sweepers, 2 bounce, 1 spot, 1 edict per deck-facts, so there is one answer per class, not two.

Against the fast seat. Take the control chair. Propaganda taxes each attacker {2}; Aetherize bounces a whole attack; Misleading Signpost moves one attacker at instant speed and then taps for {U}; every Thopter is a flying chump blocker. Spend life while the count climbs, and keep the fliers attacking the seat that cannot block them, because banked damage wins the race that arrives unannounced. Flip the turn a lord lands.

Against combo. Your clock is too slow to race (median kill turn 10 in the goldfish, a floor but not a fast one), so you win by disruption, and the disruption is three cards: Counterspell, Negate, and Launch Mishap for a creature or planeswalker spell only. Soul-Guide Lantern exiles a graveyard on demand. Held answers rot here; the last profitable moment is now. Shimmer Myr and Misleading Signpost let the engine run at instant speed with {U}{U} open, so holding it costs little. Say out loud that the combo seat is the table's problem and let the other two spend first.

At a precon table, the deck's intended one. Bracket floor 1, target 2, DeckCheck 30/96 at their Bracket 2. You are not the archenemy and should not become one: no infinite, no tutor, no Game Changer in the 99, and the six near-combos in combos.json (Hullbreaker Horror, Basalt Monolith, Tidespout Tyrant, The One Ring, Enter the Infinite, Clock of Omens) are a do-not-add list. Which card flips which matchup: Propaganda flips the fast seat; Counterspell flips combo and the wrath; Sculptor and Inspector flip the tax seat; Whirler Rogue flips the stalled board (stack 002).
